attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you update the argument in the percentChance code so that the ice cream image only appears 50% of the time when the A button is pressed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which argument determines how likely the ice cream image will appear on the screen?


Solution: 

The argument in percentChance of the if condition should be changed from 100 to 50.

﻿
steps.instructions:
Every time the A button is pressed, the ice cream image appears!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the ice cream present is selected 50% of the time when the A button is pressed.

subgroups.title: Debugging Nested Block Statements and If/Else If/Else Conditionals
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: Change argument in first percentChance code from 100 to 50.
validationItems.failureText: Check the argument used in the percentChance code.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ How should the second condition be typed in the code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What keywords should be used for the second condition in the if/else conditional?


Solution: 

if/else should be changed to else if in the controller.A block statement.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the A button is pressed, the project checks to see if the first condition is true, then moves on to the second condition if false.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check each condition to make sure that the block statements are inside curly brackets { }?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbol should be placed at the end of the else if condition’s block statement?


Solution: 

A closing curly bracket } should be added to the left of the else keyword on line 138.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 138: a declaration or statement was expected.



Fix the bugs in the code so that curly brackets are used correctly for all 3 conditions.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓ Where should game.reset() be placed so that the project resets after the present is revealed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ When does the game.reset() code currently run? When should the game be reset?


Solution: 

game.reset() should be moved inside the controller.A block statement, underneath the  pause code.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, it’s reset before the present is shown!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the project resets after the present is revealed.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about conditionals and nested block statements. Nested block statements are created when code inside of curly brackets is placed inside of another chunk of code in curly brackets, such as placing a conditional inside of a forever loop. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Curly Brackets All the Way Down
badges.description: Use nested block statements to place one block statement inside another in JavaScript.

badges.title: If at First You Don’t Succeed
badges.description: Use  “if” and “if / else” statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: ...or Else
badges.description: Use an “else if” statement in JavaScript.

badges.title: Until the End of Time
badges.description: Use a forever loop in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hey I’m Walking Here
badges.description: Use the overlapsWith function to see if two sprites are overlapping.

badges.title: Gaming the System
badges.description: Use the setGameOverEffect and gameOver functions to customize game over screens.

badges.title: The Final Countdown
badges.description: Use the info.onCountdownEnd function to run code when the countdown reaches zero.

badges.title: Playing the Odds
badges.description: Use the Math.percentChance function inside an if statement to add randomness to a project.

badges.title: A Flair for the Dramatic
badges.description: Add a custom sprite effect to a sprite.

badges.title: Let’s Try That Again
badges.description: Use the game.reset function to restart a project.
